mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates easier monetary conditions, which may stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 60% of the 20-day windows following a federal funds rate decline.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following an unemployment rate increase.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth coupled with low unemployment indicates a robust labor market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following strong employment growth and low unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate may signal tighter monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following a federal funds rate increase above 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests strong economic activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following an increase in industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real personal consumption expenditures may indicate weak demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following a decline in real personal consumption expenditures.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth without corresponding employment growth may indicate inefficiency, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following GDP growth without employment growth.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index above target inflation levels may lead to tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following a CPI increase above 2% YoY.
